nodes.summary: Gillis–Vavasis Lemma 1 (`f = ‖·‖²`), equality case: for linearly independent vectors of norm at most `M > 0`, a sub-convex combination of norm `M` is a vertex `w k` with `‖w k‖ = M`.
nodes.title: Equality case of the sub-convex combination norm bound

nodes.summary: SPA runs of every length exist (on a nonempty set of columns).
nodes.title: Existence of successive projection runs of every length

nodes.summary: `S` (most recent pick first) is a run of the successive projection algorithm: each pick maximizes the residual norm given the earlier picks (ties broken arbitrarily).
nodes.title: Run of the successive projection algorithm

nodes.summary: SPA recovers archetypes (Gillis–Vavasis Theorem 1, noiseless case): in the first `r` picks of any SPA run on a separable matrix with `r` archetypes, the picked columns are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: SPA recovers archetypes

nodes.summary: SPA recovers archetypes (Gillis–Vavasis Theorem 1, noiseless case): each of the first `r` picks of any SPA run is an archetype.
nodes.title: SPA recovers archetypes

nodes.summary: Gillis–Vavasis Lemma 1 (`f = ‖·‖²`), bound: a sub-convex combination of vectors of norm at most `M` has norm at most `M`.
nodes.title: Norm bound for a sub-convex combination of vectors

nodes.summary: After exactly `r` picks, SPA has found every archetype.
nodes.title: Successive projection finds every archetype after r picks

nodes.summary: The residual of column `j`: its projection onto the orthogonal complement of the span of the columns indexed by `S`.
nodes.title: Residual of a column in the successive projection algorithm

nodes.summary: A separable data matrix: columns `m j` are sub-convex combinations of `r` linearly independent archetypes `w k`, and every archetype is a column (Gillis–Vavasis Assumption 1).
nodes.title: Separable data matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
